summary.headline: Suyog Telematics Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue INR 717 million (~INR 71.7 crore), EBITDA INR 431 million, net profit INR 153 million.
summary.overview: Management reported Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR 717 million, EBITDA of INR 431 million (about 60% margin) and net profit of INR 153 million (21.4% margin), with EPS of INR 13.09. Revenue per tower was about INR 30,000 per month, marginally lower because most Vodafone Idea rollouts landed late in the quarter and will be billed fully from Q3. Vodafone Idea's share of revenue rose to about 31% in Q2 (30% in H1) while BSNL fell to 1.1%. Management said Vodafone Idea and BSNL tenancy adds were slower than the June 2026 order flow implied, and BSNL work worth about INR 30 crore is unbilled pending site integration.

segments.commentary: 6,263 towers and 7,674 tenancies at end Q2; 356 new Vodafone Idea tenancies added in H1 and ~150 BSNL tenancies built but not counted. Revenue per tower ~INR 30,000 per month.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 CapEx target about INR 200 crore, translating to about 2,000 tenancies, per management; to be updated monthly as operator confirmations arrive.

Management targets a quarterly revenue run-rate of INR 100 crore by September 2027; said current quarterly revenue is ~INR 75 crore, adding ~INR 15 crore per quarter (analyst computed ~INR 71.7 crore Q2 core revenue, management cited a 5-10% growth).
Vodafone Idea 45,000-site rollout over three years; Suyog targets ~5,000 sites in the next 2-3 years. Final Vodafone guidance for the next few quarters was still awaited as of the call.
Management expects ~INR 30 crore of BSNL billing to start in Q3-Q4 FY27 and BSNL pending sites to be completed by December 2026.
FY27 CapEx budget ~INR 200 crore: INR 120 crore from internal accruals and INR 80+ crore from sanctioned ICICI Bank debt. FY28 plans exist but not yet declared.
capex_capacity: H1 FY27 CapEx primarily for Vodafone Idea rollout; 356 Vodafone tenancies added and billing started for all of them within about 30 days of RFI.
BSNL: ~INR 30 crore of CapEx spent on ~300 sites that are RFI-ready but not yet billed; BSNL integration delayed by Tejas equipment and fibre issues.
Capital work-in-progress closing ~INR 87-88 crore per analyst; ~INR 20-25 crore capitalised in the period (per analyst reading).
Capacity: management said it can deliver about 1,000+ sites per month across India; ~2,000+ Vodafone sites on list, with 600 Vodafone sites under LOI with site owners.
Management says CapEx is deployed only after a service order is received; MSA lock-in of 10 years with exit charges equal to 10 years of payments.
demand_pricing: Vodafone Idea received a 600+ site order around 15 June 2026; about 150 sites delivered within 15 days and ~200+ tenancies added in Q2 per management, versus ~600-700 expected by analysts.
Business model: IP fee, site rental (reimbursed), loading charges and electricity/diesel (reimbursed) under 15-20 year MSAs with 2.5% annual escalation on IP fee and loading charges.
Loading charges for Bharti Airtel upgrades about INR 2,500 per site; last year's upgrades lifted realisation from ~INR 28,000 to ~INR 30,000 per tower.
Management says Vodafone Idea and BSNL rollout depends on operator monthly and quarterly funding; delivery capacity not the constraint.
Management noted BSNL's delay as a risk: BSNL has not started billing on ~1,800 sites handled in total, with about 50% already billing per management.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the INR 200+ crore CapEx is for Vodafone vs BSNL, and what if customer commitments do not materialise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said CapEx is deployed only after a service order; Vodafone CapEx is billed within ~30 days; ~INR 30 crore of BSNL CapEx (~300 sites) is unbilled pending integration. MSAs have 10-year lock-ins with exit charges equal to 10 years of payments.

qa_highlights.question: Why only ~206 Vodafone tenancies converted in Q2 versus 600-700 ordered, and is the 3,000-3,500 sites per month target confirmed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Vodafone releases orders monthly or quarterly and it cannot build without integration confirmation; 600 sites have LOIs. The 45,000-site three-year rollout is confirmed, but monthly phasing will vary with Vodafone funding. Final near-term guidance was still awaited.

qa_highlights.question: How is the INR 200 crore FY27 CapEx funded, and what is the debt?
qa_highlights.answer: INR 120 crore from internal accruals and INR 80+ crore of sanctioned debt from ICICI Bank. FY28 expected debt not given (first FY27 planning).

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 100 crore quarterly revenue target on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said revenue has moved from ~INR 60 crore to ~INR 75 crore per quarter and expects ~INR 15 crore per quarter additions, with INR 100 crore per quarter targeted by September 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Will BSNL compensate for billing delay, and when will the 300 sites be billed?
qa_highlights.answer: MSA requires payment from RFI date with at most a 60-day waiver; no compensation decided. Sites expected deployed by December; billing expected Q3-Q4 FY27; rent to site owners on hold until integration.

qa_highlights.question: What is H2 revenue expectation?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to INR 200 crore H2 CapEx (~2,000 sites) x ~INR 30,000 monthly per tower as a rough calculation, with shortfall possible on operator plans.

risks_watch: Vodafone Idea rollout pace depends on its funding tranches; monthly and quarterly phasing not yet confirmed; final guidance awaited.
BSNL: ~INR 30 crore CapEx (~300 sites) unbilled; billing dependent on Tejas equipment and fibre resolution; billing timing shifted to Q3-Q4 FY27.
Balance-sheet and funding: management gave only INR 200 crore FY27 CapEx split (INR 120 crore internal accruals, INR 80+ crore ICICI debt); FY27/28 debt level not disclosed.
Gap between CapEx deployed and tenancy additions: analysts flagged ~INR 150 crore of CapEx since FY26 vs ~400-500 tenancies added.
Quarterly revenue growth has been slow (~1% QoQ in Q2 on analyst numbers) versus the INR 100 crore per quarter target by September 2027.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the business model, CapEx-to-service-order discipline and contract terms, but evasive and inconsistent on tenancy and revenue timing, with several answers deferred to future operator confirmations. Management repeatedly qualified targets as dependent on operator plans.
key_quotes: We don't invest a single rupee without getting one service order from any of the operators.
45,000 is their confirmed rollout which they have declared on public platform also and that data is also with us also.
BSNL is to pay me from RFI date maximum 60 days waiver is allowed after which my billing starts automatically and BSNL will have to pay me as per MSA.
So, delivery is not an issue for Suyog.

adds.what: ~2,000 tenancies in H2 FY27 funded by ~INR 200 crore CapEx (Vodafone Idea and BSNL rollouts)
~5,000 Vodafone Idea sites targeted over next 2-3 years
~300 BSNL sites RFI-ready but not yet billed (~INR 30 crore already spent)

growth.why: Management targets ~INR 200 crore capex in H2 FY27 (~2,000 tenancies) and a INR 100 crore quarterly revenue run-rate by September 2027 (cut from earlier timing), but Vodafone Idea tenancy adds (356 in H1 vs ~3,000 guided) and BSNL billing have lagged, and Q2 revenue grew only ~1% QoQ.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management guided ~INR 200 crore H2 FY27 CapEx (~2,000 tenancies) funded by INR 120 crore internal accruals and INR 80+ crore sanctioned ICICI debt, but CapEx is only deployed after service orders, so timing depends on operator orders.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Only 356 Vodafone tenancies added in H1 versus 600-700 expected from the June order, and BSNL's ~300 RFI-ready sites are unbilled; quarterly revenue grew only ~1% QoQ to ~INR 71.7 crore, so growth hinges on Vodafone and BSNL funding and integration.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says FY28 plans exist but are undeclared, and the 45,000-site Vodafone rollout and ~5,000-site Suyog target over 2-3 years require further capex; capacity is 1,000+ sites a month, so the pipeline is not constrained by delivery.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management cut the INR 100 crore quarterly revenue target timing to September 2027 and Q2 revenue was only ~INR 71.7 crore, far from that run-rate, so an upgrade is not indicated.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Vodafone final guidance is still awaited, BSNL billing has slipped to Q3-Q4 FY27 on ~INR 30 crore of unbilled CapEx, and H2 tenancy target of ~2,000 depends on operator confirmations.

rows.label: BSNL ~INR 30 crore billing start
rows.why: Management expects ~INR 30 crore of BSNL billing once ~300 RFI-ready sites are integrated, with sites due to be completed by December 2026, though Tejas equipment and fibre issues have already delayed it.

rows.label: Realisation uplift from Bharti upgrades
rows.why: Last year's upgrades lifted realisation from ~INR 28,000 to ~INR 30,000 per tower, and loading charges are ~INR 2,500 per site, but Q2 realisation slipped to ~INR 30,000 from ~INR 31,000 as Vodafone rollouts landed late.

rows.label: Debt-funded CapEx from ICICI Bank
rows.why: INR 80+ crore of sanctioned ICICI debt funds part of the INR 200 crore FY27 CapEx, with INR 120 crore from internal accruals; FY27/28 debt level not disclosed.

tone.note: Management was confident on the business model, CapEx-to-service-order discipline and 10-year MSA lock-ins, but cautious on Vodafone and BSNL tenancy timing; analysts probed the gap between 600-700 expected and 206 converted Vodafone tenancies, plus the slow revenue growth.
